title: Equipment Checks, Mounting, and Labeling

sections.learningObjectives:
- Verify ECG equipment readiness, including power, supplies, electrodes, cables, paper, and calibration, before a recording and act on expired, damaged, or missing items.
- Mount a completed ECG tracing flat, complete, and legible into the correct patient's record while preserving identifiers and the calibration mark.
- Label each tracing with at least two patient-specific identifiers plus the correct date, time, and ordering clinician, without guessing or pre-labeling.
- Recognize common ECG artifacts and equipment problems and apply basic troubleshooting, escalating rather than interpreting.
- Escalate equipment malfunctions, uncertain tracings, and patient symptoms to licensed staff and follow office policy at all times.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Checking the machine first is like checking that a pencil is sharpened before a test starts, so you are not scrambling when it is time to write.

### Question 2

Using expired sticky patches is like trying to use old, dried-out glue; it will not stick or work the way it should.

### Question 3

A dried-out electrode is like a dried-out marker; it cannot do its job, so you reach for a fresh one.

### Question 4

A frayed wire is like a cracked hose; patching it with tape is not a real fix, so you get a new one.

### Question 5

The cable is the pathway that carries the heart's electrical 'message' from the sticky patches to the machine, like a phone cord carrying your voice.

### Question 6

Having paper ready is like putting a fresh roll in a camera before a trip, so you do not miss the moment.

### Question 7

The calibration mark is like the 'zero' line on a ruler; it tells the reader that the measuring tool was set up correctly before it was used.

### Question 8

Running the machine's self-check is like doing a quick test run of a car's lights before a long drive, so you know it works.

### Question 9

Checking the battery is like making sure your tablet is charged before a long car ride.

### Question 10

Keeping electrodes sealed is like keeping a glue stick capped so it does not dry out.

### Question 11

Setting up early is like laying out all the ingredients before you start baking, so everything is ready when you need it.

### Question 12

Wiping the equipment between patients is like washing your hands between tasks, so you do not pass germs from one person to the next.

### Question 13

Reporting a broken machine is like telling a grown-up when a toy stops working instead of trying to take it apart yourself.

### Question 14

Having all the patches and wires ready is like making sure every piece of a puzzle is in the box before you start.

### Question 15

The assistant checks that the camera works; the doctor is the one who reads the photo and says what it means.

### Question 16

Setting the clock correctly is like putting the right time stamp on a photo so you know exactly when it was taken.

### Question 17

Getting all the sticky patches ready is like setting out a full set of colored markers, not just one color.

### Question 18

Throwing away expired supplies is like not eating food past its 'use by' date, because it might not work the way it should.

### Question 19

Other buzzing machines nearby can add 'static' to the recording, like a radio picking up crackle from a nearby fan.

### Question 20

Keeping a log is like writing down what you did and what broke so you can remember and fix things faster next time.

### Question 21

Tucking cords away is like picking up toys from the floor so nobody trips over them.

### Question 22

A checklist is like a pilot's pre-flight list that makes sure every important thing is checked before takeoff.

### Question 23

Getting the missing piece first is like finishing a full set of batteries before starting a project.

### Question 24

Clean, dry skin is like a clean, dry wall before you stick on a hook, so it stays put.

### Question 25

Making sure everything is ready first is like checking you have all the ingredients before you start cooking.

### Question 26

Sticking the patches down firmly is like pressing a sticker all the way down so it does not peel up.

### Question 27

Using the standard settings is like using the same ruler every time so measurements always match.

### Question 28

Clearing the last person's info is like erasing a whiteboard before a new lesson so the old notes do not get mixed in.

### Question 29

Laying the paper flat in the right folder is like putting a photo straight into the right family album so it does not get crumpled or lost.

### Question 30

Checking whose paper it is before filing is like checking the name on a homework sheet before handing it in, so it goes to the right person.

### Question 31

Keeping the calibration mark is like keeping the 'scale' line on a map so the reader knows the distances are true.

### Question 32

If a picture comes out blurry, you take it again instead of gluing the blurry one in the album.

### Question 33

Filing the paper right away is like putting your drawing in your folder immediately so it does not get mixed with a friend's.

### Question 34

Putting the strips in the right order is like arranging pages of a story in order so it can be read from start to finish.

### Question 35

Keeping the paper whole is like not cutting pieces off a photo, so you can still see the whole picture.

### Question 36

Sticking the paper down firmly is like using a paperclip so an important note stays with the right packet.

### Question 37

If the photocopy is too light to read, you make a new copy instead of writing over it.

### Question 38

Putting the paper in its proper spot is like putting each book back on its labeled shelf so it can be found again.

### Question 39

Holding the paper by its edges is like holding a fresh drawing by the corners so you do not smudge the middle.

### Question 40

Checking the name, date, and time is like checking the name and date at the top of a letter before you file it.

### Question 41

If a page rips, you print a fresh copy instead of taping the torn one back together.

### Question 42

Keeping each person's papers separate is like keeping each student's tests in their own folder so nobody gets the wrong grade.

### Question 43

Keeping the name label visible is like keeping the name tag on a backpack where you can still read it.

### Question 44

Filing the paper in the record is like adding a page to a book so the whole story stays together.

### Question 45

Letting ink dry is like waiting for paint to dry before touching it, so it does not smear.

### Question 46

Keeping each paper with its own date is like keeping dated diary pages in order so you know which day each one belongs to.

### Question 47

Labeling with two identifiers is like writing both a name and a class number on a project so it cannot be confused with anyone else's.

### Question 48

Writing the date and time is like stamping a photo with when it was taken.

### Question 49

Writing the doctor's name on the paper is like writing the teacher's name on homework so it gets to the right desk.

### Question 50

Copying from the label on the folder is like reading the name right off a library card instead of guessing.

### Question 51

If you are not sure of a name, you check the list instead of writing a guess.

### Question 52

Fixing a mistake the right way is like crossing out one word and writing the correct one so everyone can still see what happened.

### Question 53

A medical record number is like a student ID number, unique to one person.

### Question 54

You would never write a friend's name on your own test paper; each person's name belongs only on their own work.

### Question 55

Labeling right away is like writing your name on your drawing as soon as you finish it, before it gets mixed up.

### Question 56

Making sure the label matches the chart is like checking that the name on a folder matches the paper inside it.

### Question 57

The assistant writes down what they saw, like 'the patient was lying down,' but lets the doctor decide what it means.

### Question 58

Writing clearly is like writing neatly on an envelope so the mail carrier can read the address.

### Question 59

If you are not sure whose test it is, you stop and ask the teacher instead of writing any name down.

### Question 60

The label is like the name tag on a lunchbox, making sure the right person gets their own food.

### Question 61

Writing the full name is like writing your complete name on an important form, not just your nickname.

### Question 62

The time on the label should be like the exact time stamp on a text message, showing when it really happened.

### Question 63

Putting your name on every page of a report is like writing your name on each page so none of them get lost.

### Question 64

Writing the name before the person arrives is like writing a name on a test before you know whose test it is.

### Question 65

A wandering line is like a shaky line drawn while the paper is moving; staying still makes the line smoother.

### Question 66

Shaky little spikes are like a wobbly line drawn while your hand is shivering from the cold.

### Question 67

The fuzzy pattern is like static on a radio from another machine nearby, not the song itself.

### Question 68

A flat line on one wire usually means that patch came unplugged, so you plug it back in, like reconnecting a loose headphone.

### Question 69

If every line goes flat at once, it is like the whole microphone got unplugged, so you check the main cord first.

### Question 70

If a sticker will not stick, you clean the spot and use a fresh sticker instead of hoping it stays.

### Question 71

Artifact is like a smudge on a photo, not part of the actual picture you are trying to see.

### Question 72

If the picture is blurry, you retake it instead of guessing what it shows.

### Question 73

Moving during the recording is like wiggling while someone takes your picture, which makes it blurry.

### Question 74

If you tried twice and it still will not work, you ask the teacher for help instead of trying forever alone.

### Question 75

It is like knowing the difference between fixing a loose button yourself and telling a grown-up when someone feels unwell.

### Question 76

If a camera keeps taking blurry photos no matter what, you send it to be fixed instead of keeping it in use.

### Question 77

Checking the stickers first is like checking the plugs when a lamp flickers, before assuming the bulb is the problem.

### Question 78

Telling the right person when equipment breaks is like telling the teacher when the classroom computer stops working.

### Question 79

The assistant can say 'the doctor will read it and explain it to you,' like a photographer who hands the picture to the doctor to read.

### Question 80

If someone says their chest hurts, you tell the doctor right away, just like telling a teacher when a friend feels sick.

### Question 81

Giving the finished paper to the doctor is like handing your homework to the teacher to be checked.

### Question 82

When you are not sure, asking a grown-up for help is always the safe choice.

### Question 83

Reading the squiggly lines is the doctor's job, like a referee being the one who calls the game, not the person holding the score sheet.

### Question 84

Writing down a small problem is like telling someone about a small leak so it can be fixed before it becomes a big one.

### Question 85

If someone feels sick and the machine breaks, you help the person first and tell the doctor, then worry about the machine.
